documents.informedConsent.title: Informed Consent
documents.informedConsent.subtitle: Mandibular Advancement Devices (MAD) for Patients
documents.informedConsent.intro: NeoSleep is a network of dental sleep specialists in Mexico and Spain that coordinates, for patients with Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) and snoring, the assessment, treatment, and follow-up with Mandibular Advancement Devices (MAD). NeoSleep is not a manufacturer of these devices: it acts as an intermediary between you, the treating dental specialist, and the manufacturer/laboratory responsible for designing and manufacturing the custom-made device.
documents.informedConsent.p1: Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) and snoring are respiratory disorders that occur repeatedly during sleep due to total obstruction (apnea) or narrowing of the upper airway, caused by the position and tension of the muscles involved in the passage of air through the upper airway. The main symptoms of Obstructive Sleep Apnea are snoring, breathing pauses during sleep, daytime sleepiness, fatigue, etc.
documents.informedConsent.p2: OSA can pose serious health risks, as it disrupts normal sleep patterns and can reduce normal blood oxygen levels. This condition can increase the risk of daytime sleepiness, fatigue, headaches, traffic and workplace accidents, hypertension (high blood pressure), heart disease, heart attacks, strokes, diabetes, obesity, memory and learning problems, and depression.
documents.informedConsent.p3: In any case, it is recommended to follow the hygiene and dietary measures your specialist has informed you about.
documents.informedConsent.p4: This informed consent refers to MAD treatments coordinated through NeoSleep.
documents.informedConsent.p5: MAD therapy for OSA and snoring aims to ease breathing by keeping the tongue and jaw in an advanced position during sleep. MADs are clinically proven and highly effective; however, there is no guarantee that the treatment will be effective in your particular case. Every patient is different, and many factors influence the upper airway during sleep. It is important to recognize that, even when the therapy is effective, there may be a period during which symptoms related to your sleep-disordered breathing persist. For this reason, several follow-up visits with your NeoSleep specialist may be necessary to adjust the degree of mandibular advancement.
documents.informedConsent.p6: A polygraphy or polysomnography (sleep study) may be performed after the adjustment to objectively confirm the effectiveness of the treatment. You should request this from your specialist.
documents.informedConsent.p7: MADs are indicated for patients with mild to moderate obstructive sleep apnea, and in severe cases where there is intolerance to other treatments. They are also indicated for patients who snore. Their use is contraindicated in patients with central sleep apnea, other respiratory diseases, advanced periodontal problems, and in patients under 18 years of age.
documents.informedConsent.p8: This is a reversible treatment: it is only effective while worn in the mouth and can be discontinued at any time (unlike surgical treatment). If you stop using it, OSA symptoms and/or snoring may return.
documents.informedConsent.p9: Side effects of MADs. Published scientific studies show that short-term side effects of MAD treatment may include excessive salivation, difficulty swallowing (while the device is in place), jaw or tooth pain, jaw joint pain, dry mouth, gum pain, tooth movement, and short-term bite changes. Most of these side effects are mild and resolve on their own or with a minor adjustment of the device. Studies also exist on the loosening of dental restorations (crowns, implants, etc.).
documents.informedConsent.p10: Long-term complications include bite changes that, in some cases, may be permanent, as a result of tooth movement or repositioning of the jaw joint. These complications may or may not be fully reversible once treatment with oral devices is discontinued. If they are not reversible, restorative treatment or orthodontic intervention may be necessary, for which you will be responsible.
documents.informedConsent.p11: Follow-up visits with your NeoSleep specialist are mandatory to ensure correct adjustment of the device and the effectiveness of the treatment. If unusual symptoms or discomfort occur that fall outside the scope of this consent, or if pain relievers are needed to manage discomfort, it is recommended to stop using the device until a further evaluation is carried out.
documents.informedConsent.p12: In exceptional cases, you may experience nausea, difficulty falling asleep, or accidentally swallow a part of the device.
documents.informedConsent.declareBody: that I have been informed about OSA, the treatment alternatives, MAD treatment, and the possible side effects, discomfort, and complications that may arise from its use. I am aware that the treatment may not be fully effective in my case and that it is my responsibility to inform my NeoSleep specialist of any side effects and of how my symptoms evolve. I am also aware that not treating sleep-related breathing disorders may increase the likelihood of significant medical complications.
documents.informedConsent.declareBody2: All doubts or questions I have had regarding the treatment, its risks, and its complications have been satisfactorily answered and clarified.
documents.informedConsent.authorizeBody: the treating dental specialist and their team, as well as NeoSleep in its role as treatment coordinator, to collect the information necessary (records, measurements, photographs, videos, X-rays, etc.) to carry out my MAD treatment.
documents.informedConsent.authorizeBody2: I authorize the transmission of that information, exclusively for the design and manufacture of the custom-made device, to the manufacturer/laboratory responsible for it, marked below by my NeoSleep specialist:
documents.informedConsent.authorizeBody3: I further authorize all parties — the treating specialist, NeoSleep, and the manufacturer — to use the information collected for research or scientific-disclosure purposes, guaranteeing my anonymity at all times.
documents.informedConsent.revokeNotice: You reserve the right to revoke this consent, without needing to provide any justification, at any time before the procedure or treatment described is carried out.

website.privacy.title: Privacy Policy
website.privacy.intro: {company} respects your privacy and is committed to protecting your personal data. This policy explains what personal data we collect through this website, how we use it, and what rights you have.
website.privacy.s1.title: Who we are
website.privacy.s1.body: {legalEntityName} ({company}), with registered address at {address}, is the data controller responsible for the personal data collected through this website. For any privacy-related question, contact us at {email}.
website.privacy.s2.title: Data we collect
website.privacy.s2.body: We collect only the data you voluntarily provide through this website: first and last name, phone number, email address, city, and a description of your symptoms or treatment needs, when you use our specialist-matching or booking tools. If you are a dental professional registering interest as a partner clinic, we also collect your clinic name, tax identification number, and billing address.
website.privacy.s3.title: How we use your data, and our legal basis
website.privacy.s3.body: We use your data to match you with a certified specialist in your area, respond to your enquiry, and, if you agree, contact you about your request. The legal basis for this processing is the performance of pre-contractual steps taken at your request (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR) and, where applicable, your explicit consent (Art. 6(1)(a) and, for health-related information, Art. 9(2)(a) GDPR). We do not use your data for any purpose incompatible with these.
website.privacy.s4.title: Who we share your data with
website.privacy.s4.body: We share your data only with the certified specialist handling your enquiry and with service providers who process data on our behalf under a data processing agreement (for example, hosting, email delivery, and scheduling providers). We never sell your data or share it with third parties for their own marketing purposes.
website.privacy.s5.title: International data transfers
website.privacy.s5.body: Some of our service providers may process data outside the European Economic Area. Where this happens, we rely on appropriate safeguards recognised under GDPR, such as the European Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses. You can request more information about these safeguards by contacting us at {email}.
website.privacy.s6.title: How long we keep your data
website.privacy.s6.body: We retain your data for as long as necessary for the purpose it was collected, and in any case no longer than 3 years from your last contact with us, unless a longer period is required by law. Data related to an active treatment relationship is retained for the duration of that relationship.
website.privacy.s7.title: Your rights
website.privacy.s7.body: You have the right to access, rectify, erase, restrict, and object to the processing of your data, and to data portability, under Articles 15–21 GDPR. You may withdraw consent at any time without affecting the lawfulness of processing carried out before withdrawal. To exercise any of these rights, contact us at {email}. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with {authorityName}.
website.privacy.s8.title: Cookies
website.privacy.s8.body: We only use essential technical cookies required for this website to function. We do not use third-party advertising or tracking cookies. You can manage cookies through your browser settings.
website.privacy.s9.title: Changes to this policy & contact
website.privacy.s9.body: We may update this policy from time to time. Significant changes will be communicated by email or via a notice on this website. For any privacy-related enquiry, contact {legalEntityName} at {email} or {address}.

website.help.faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
website.help.faq.q1.a: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a sleep disorder in which the throat muscles intermittently relax and block the upper airway during sleep, causing breathing to repeatedly stop and restart. It affects an estimated 1 billion people worldwide and is associated with serious health risks including hypertension, cardiovascular disease, and cognitive impairment.
website.help.faq.q2.q: What are the main warning signs?
website.help.faq.q2.a: The most common signs include loud or frequent snoring, gasping or choking sounds during sleep, excessive daytime sleepiness, morning headaches, dry mouth on waking, and difficulty concentrating. A partner or family member often notices the breathing pauses before the patient does.
website.help.faq.q3.q: How does an oral appliance treat sleep apnea?
website.help.faq.q3.a: A custom-fitted mandibular advancement device (MAD) gently repositions the lower jaw and tongue forward, keeping the upper airway open during sleep. It is worn like a sports mouthguard, requires no mask or machine, and is clinically validated for mild-to-moderate OSA. Many patients find it more comfortable and easier to travel with than CPAP therapy.
website.help.faq.q4.q: When can I expect to see results?
website.help.faq.q4.a: Most patients report noticeable improvements in sleep quality and daytime alertness within the first one to two weeks. Full adaptation to the appliance typically takes two to four weeks. A follow-up appointment at six to eight weeks allows your specialist to fine-tune the fit and confirm treatment efficacy.
website.help.faq.q5.q: How do I join the NeoSleep specialist network?
website.help.faq.q5.a: Any dentist interested in dental sleep medicine is welcome to join — no specialization is required. Complete the contact form on our website and select the 'Professional' option. A member of our team will reach out within two business days to walk you through the onboarding process, training programme, and platform setup. No upfront fees are required to apply.
website.help.faq.q6.q: What training and certification does NeoSleep provide?
website.help.faq.q6.a: We offer a structured dental sleep medicine certification programme covering OSA screening protocols, appliance selection and titration, patient communication, and follow-up care. Existing accreditations (ABDSM, SomnoMed, etc.) are recognised and may reduce the required training hours. Continuing education credits are available upon completion.
website.help.faq.q7.q: How is my personal and health data protected?
website.help.faq.q7.a: All data is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.3) and at rest (AES-256). We comply with GDPR (EU), LFPDPPP (Mexico), and PDPA (Thailand). Your health information is only accessible to you and the licensed specialist managing your case. We never sell or share your data with third parties for commercial purposes.
website.help.faq.q8.q: Can I request deletion of my data?
website.help.faq.q8.a: Yes. You have the right to erasure under GDPR and equivalent laws in other jurisdictions. To submit a deletion request, send an email to info@neosleepcare.com with the subject 'Data Deletion Request'. We will process your request within 30 days and confirm once complete.
website.help.cta.heading: Didn't find your answer?
website.help.cta.subtitle: Our team is ready to help. Send us a message and we'll get back to you shortly.
